title: What if we aimed the Hubble Telescope at Earth?

A_identity.core_topic: What Hubble would actually see if pointed at Earth's surface, and why.
A_identity.audience_inferred: Curious general viewers with casual interest in space and physics; no maths needed (inferred from plain vocabulary).
A_identity.primary_question: How detailed would Hubble's images of Earth be?
A_identity.promise: A real answer to a commonly asked question, with the true limiting factor explained.
A_identity.style: Dry, conversational first-person explanation with running concrete example (a desk).
A_identity.pov: First-person narrator answering a named reader; 'we' for the thought experiment.

B_hook.opening_quote: If the Hubble telescope were aimed at the Earth, how detailed would the images be?
B_hook.construction: Reader question, then social proof that it is commonly asked, then a popular wrong answer is dismissed, then the one-line true cause, then 'Let me explain'.
B_hook.first_curiosity_trigger: The claim that the cause is slowness, which is not the reason most people would guess.
B_hook.conflict_or_contradiction: The popular explanation (Earth too bright) is stated and rejected with a named source.
B_hook.withheld: What 'too slow' means, what the picture would look like, and whether the problem can be fixed.
B_hook.audience_expectation: Viewer expects a quick image-quality verdict; gets a diagnosis that needs unpacking.
B_hook.promise_strength_reason: States the answer's cause in one sentence and explicitly commits to explaining it.
B_hook.opening_to_payoff: 'Too slow' is restated near the end with the rotation numbers, then overturned by the spy-satellite reveal.
B_hook.why_may_hold: Correcting a common belief may plausibly create a need to hear the real reason.
B_hook.weaknesses: Several sentences of sourcing (FAQ, Bad Astronomy) come before any vivid image; 'too slow' is abstract until much later.

F_mechanics.quote: The fundamental problem is that Hubble is too slow. Let me explain.
F_mechanics.construction: One-clause diagnosis plus an explicit explain promise.
F_mechanics.function: Gives the answer label while withholding its meaning.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May keep watching to decode the label.
F_mechanics.reuse: State the cause in five words, then say you will explain.

F_mechanics.quote: Let’s imagine we want to take a photo of this normal desk.
F_mechanics.construction: One mundane object reused at every stage of degradation.
F_mechanics.function: Makes each abstract limit a visible before/after.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: Plausibly easier to follow and compare stages.
F_mechanics.reuse: Pick one ordinary object and re-test it after each new factor.

F_mechanics.quote: But the big problem is motion: Hubble is moving across Earth’s surface at over 7 kilometers per second.
F_mechanics.construction: 'First small problem' set up earlier, then 'But the big problem'.
F_mechanics.function: Ranks obstacles so the script escalates.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May signal the main point is arriving.
F_mechanics.reuse: Label obstacles small/big and order them ascending.

F_mechanics.quote: trying to take a picture of the ground passing beneath your car
F_mechanics.construction: Everyday equivalent placed right after the technical claim.
F_mechanics.function: Translates orbital motion blur into familiar experience.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May produce an instant 'I get it'.
F_mechanics.reuse: Follow each technical claim with a same-problem everyday case.

F_mechanics.quote: Could we rotate Hubble to track the surface, and eliminate the blur?
F_mechanics.construction: Voices the viewer's obvious objection as a question.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May feel the script anticipated their thought.
F_mechanics.reuse: After a negative result, ask the obvious fix out loud.

F_mechanics.quote: about the speed of a minute hand on a clock
F_mechanics.construction: Parenthetical everyday yardstick for a rotation rate.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May make the slowness feel absurd.
F_mechanics.reuse: Attach a household-speed comparison to every rate.

F_mechanics.quote: But this isn’t just a hypothetical situation.
F_mechanics.construction: After the payoff, a 'But' flips the frame from fantasy to fact.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May cause surprise and mild unease.
F_mechanics.reuse: End a hypothetical by showing where it already exists.

H_pacing.sequencing: Problem, attempted fix, new problem, fix, verdict, twist.

H_pacing.setup_to_payoff: Each sub-problem pays off within a few sentences; the main answer arrives near the end.
H_pacing.slow_sections: The atmosphere digression and the Moon-tracking detail.

H_pacing.weaknesses: Several payoffs depend on unseen images ('looks like this'), so the text alone is thin there.
H_pacing.tempo_evidence: Short verdict lines such as 'That’s no good.' alternate with multi-clause explanations.

strengths: The cause is named in the opening and paid off with numbers later.
One desk example is carried through every stage.
The ending reframes the whole hypothetical as real.
improvements: The opening could reach the 'too slow' line with less sourcing preamble.
Text payoffs that rely on 'looks like this' could carry a verbal description.
K_assessment.distinctive_technique: Naming the answer early as a cryptic label, then spending the script making the label mean something.
K_assessment.biggest_risk: Sourcing-heavy opening sentences may plausibly lose viewers before the first vivid idea.
K_assessment.lesson: An early answer does not kill curiosity if the answer itself needs explaining.

L_formula: Attribute the question to a named reader.
Dismiss the popular wrong answer with a source.
State the real cause in one cryptic line and promise to explain.
Rank obstacles small then big, re-testing the object each time.
Voice the obvious fix as a question and show why it fails.
Grant a hypothetical upgrade and give a concrete human-scale verdict.
Close by revealing the hypothetical already exists.

lenses.architect: Structure is a fix-and-fail ladder: each solution exposes the next constraint.
lenses.surgeon: The parenthetical minute-hand comparison does more work than the rpm figure before it.
lenses.viral: 'it’s what the US government actually does' is the most quotable line because it turns trivia into a slightly ominous fact.
lenses.critic: The atmosphere aside answers a question nobody in the script asked and delays the first real obstacle.
lenses.curiosity: The 'too slow' label stays undefined for most of the script, which is the main retention device in the text.
lenses.platform: The opening sentence is the search query nearly verbatim; the resolution-plus-motion block and the tracking-to-spy-satellite block each stand alone.
lenses.integrator: Humor, analogy and the running desk all serve the same job of making limits visible.
lenses.tradeoffs: Credibility sourcing up front costs hook speed; the late reveal gains surprise at the cost of not being promised.
